test_title: PYST 25: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 20 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Where is the primary focus of the Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rural areas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY)** was launched in **September 2001** by merging two earlier schemes: the Employment Assurance Scheme (EAS) and the Jawahar Gram Samridhi Yojana (JGSY).
 
• The primary focus of this scheme is on **Rural areas**, aiming to provide wage employment to the rural poor and create durable community assets.
 
• The scheme emphasizes the involvement of **Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs)** in planning and implementing projects, ensuring local participation and development.
 
• Under SGRY, wages are paid partly in cash and partly in kind (food grains), ensuring both income and food security for rural workers.
 
• The key beneficiaries of the scheme are individuals living below the poverty line in rural areas, with a special focus on women, Scheduled Castes (SCs), and Scheduled Tribes (STs).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objectives of Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY):**

 
 
• The scheme aims to provide **additional wage employment** in rural areas and ensure food security through the distribution of food grains.
 
• It focuses on creating **durable and productive community assets** like roads, irrigation canals, and school buildings in rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Funding Mechanism:**
 
 
• The scheme is funded by the **Government of India** and the respective **state governments**.
 
• The cost-sharing ratio between the Central and State governments is **75:25**.
 
• Food grains are provided free of cost to the states by the Central government as part of the scheme.
 
 
 
• **Implementation and Monitoring:**
 
 
• The scheme is implemented through **Panchayati Raj Institutions**, which play a key role in identifying local needs and executing projects.
 
• Monitoring is conducted at the **district, state, and central levels** to ensure effective implementation and transparency.
 
 
 
• **Target Beneficiaries:**
 
 
• The scheme targets rural households, especially those living below the poverty line (BPL).
 
• Special emphasis is placed on providing employment opportunities to **women**, **Scheduled Castes (SCs)**, and **Scheduled Tribes (STs)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of SGRY:**

 
 
• SGRY contributes significantly to reducing rural unemployment and ensuring food security for vulnerable sections of society.
 
• The scheme also aids in rural development through the creation of durable assets, which improve infrastructure and living standards in villages.
 
 
 
• **Transition to Other Schemes:**
 
 
• In 2006, SGRY was subsumed under the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)**, which provides a legal guarantee for 100 days of wage employment to rural households.
 
• MGNREGA expanded on the objectives of SGRY by incorporating a rights-based approach to employment and ensuring transparency and accountability in implementation.
